statement.p: Calculate the circulation, \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r, in two ways, directly and using Stokes' Theorem. The vector field \vec F = (8x-8y+7z)(\vec i+\vec j) and C is the triangle with vertices (0,0,0), (3,0,0), (3,5,0), traversed in that order.
Calculating directly, we break C into three paths. For each, give a parameterization \vec r\,(t) that traverses the path from start to end for 0\le t\le1.

static.solution:
\int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r directly, we compute the integral along each of the sides of the triangle, as indicated. On C_1, the easiest indicated parameterization is \vec r_1(t) = 3 t\vec i. On C_2 and C_3, we similarly can take \vec r_2(t) = 3\vec i + 5 t\vec j \quad\mbox{and}\quad \vec r_3(t) = 3(1 - t)\vec i + 5(1 - t)\vec j. Thus \int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1 24 t(\vec i + \vec j)\cdot(3\vec i)\,dt = \int_0^1 72\,t\,dt = 36. Similarly, \int_{C_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1 (24 - 40 t)(\vec i + \vec j)\cdot( 5\vec j)\,dt = \int_0^1 24 - 200\,t\,dt = 20, and \int_{C_3}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1 (24(1 - t) - 40(1 - t))(\vec i + \vec j)\cdot (-3\vec i - 5\vec j)\, dt = 64. Then \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r + \int_{C_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec r + \int_{C_3}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = 120.
To calculate \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r using Stokes' Theorem, we find \mbox{curl }\vec F = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \amp \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \amp \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\\ 8x-8y+7z \amp 8x-8y+7z \amp 0 \end{array}\right| = -7\vec i+ 7\vec j+ 16\vec k. For Stokes' Theorem, the triangular region S in contained by the triangle is oriented upward, so d\vec A=\vec k\,dx\,dy. Thus \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S\mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_S(-7\vec i+7\vec j+16\vec k)\cdot \vec k\, dx\, dy = \int_0^{3}\int_0^{5 x/3}\,16\,dx\,dy = 120.
